> A DIY recreation of the classic Marshall 'The Guv'nor' guitar pedal, which aims to sound similar to some of their greatest rock amps. Since the circuit uses LEDs for the distortion and clipping, I'll take advantage of them lighting up as the clipping kicks in to make a flashing, responsive light feature on the pedal!

## Design

### 2026-10-19 – New week, new project!

**1h**

New week, new project!

I have researched and planned what I'm gonna do this week.

I really liked the idea of making a talkbox, but that would be kinda expensive and pretty complex. I considered an analogue synth, but eventually decided on a guitar pedal since I could actually use it if what I make works lol

The Marshall "The Guv'nor" is what I've set my sights on recreating. A classic distortion pedal that *should* sound like classic rock amps like the JCM800. Think Green Day, The Darkness, and so many more!

Since the circuit uses LEDs for the distortion and clipping, I'll take advantage of them lighting up as the clipping kicks in to make a flashing, responsive light feature on the pedal!

Hyped to build this! Let's see how it goes...

### 2026-10-20 – Today I finalised my plans and began work on the schematic.

**1.7h**

Today I finalised my plans and began work on the schematic.

In the end, I have decided to follow this tutorial here: https://aionfx.com/app/files/docs/equinox_legacy_documentation.pdf
From this, I will copy the schematic into easyEDA, choosing the correct parts along the way. Doing it like this means that I have all the right data already embedded in the schematic, so the PCB will automatically have the right footprints. Then, when I order from LCSC, the components will be linked.

I've made good progress. I am systematically and carefully laying out the schematic and it's going well!

To make this my own, I am going to ensure the LEDs used for the audio clipping are visible, since they will light up when you play through them. Time permitting, I'll also design a basic enclosure that I can 3D print with my prize for finishing this challenge! Besides, this tutorial is mostly for if you are buying one of their pre-built PCB and component kits. I am laying it out from scratch.

### 2026-10-21 – The schematic is going well!

**1.1h**

The schematic is going well!

Despite making a PCB in week 1, I'm still kinda slow. Also, though, this is a much more complex schematic. However, I'm really enjoying it; especially hunting down the perfect components, making sure they are of course the right measurement/rating but also ensuring they are high enough quality and also affordable. Annoyingly there is not a single repeated resistor or capacitor in this build, so I'm gonna have quite a few left over at the end. But I guess that gives me some spare components for future projects!

The IC is now fully wired up (that took me a while to understand why it's 2 symbols on the schematic), and I'm about to move onto the LEDs - I think I have found a good option, but need to be sure. And since some of the sound actually comes from these LEDs (crazy huh), I need to ensure they are the perfect ones!

### 2026-10-22 – The schematic is nearly finished!

**1.9h**

The schematic is nearly finished!

Today I continued copying over and implementing the schematic. It is so satisfying when you find 100 resistors for 30 cents, nestled in between the 20 for 80 cents listings!

The bias divider and power input is in a separate, self-contained section of the schematic which is nice and tidy. It also has reverse polarity protection through D1, a 1N4001 diode, which stops electricity of the wrong polarity from entering the pedal circuits and frying them.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/8777ef1a8638b734206ea4a466b7cac4c7fde13dd7cd8edd6dd973eb6ab7196b.png)

All I have to add to the schematic now is the pots. But to do that, I need to decide where I'm going to source them from, what size I need (if that matters), and how best to implement the footprint. And I need to hunt down a 3PDT footswitch for a reasonable price lol

My cart so far:

### 2026-10-23 – # The schematic (should be) done!

**2.6h**

# The schematic (should be) done!

I have made a LOT of progress! The schematic is now fully transferred over into EasyEDA, which includes finding all the components on LCSC and using their symbols in the schematic, to avoid having to manually find any footprints. Here is the finished schematic:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/36bef67b77eec9a8deded72ba534266e0e061c719a77e44e0b4330457950fa87.png)

You will notice that I’ve had to replace the Net Ports for the audio/power/switch connections with basic generic 1-hole pads. This is so that EasyEDA can automatically show me the connections to make between these and the circuit, so I can decide where to put the holes I will eventually solder these wires onto.

I also spent a considerable amount of time trying to find the right pots and power jack. LCSC just didn’t stock the kind of pots I needed (10k log, 100k linear), or at least not for a reasonable price. And as far as I could see, they didn’t stock some of the other pedal-specific parts either. So I spent a while finding the sites with the best balance of cost and delivery. I think I’ve found one in bitsboxuk, but will try again one more time with LCSC tomorrow.

### 2026-10-24 – THE PCB IS DONE!

**2.62h**

THE PCB IS DONE!

Today, I *LOCKED IN*. I imported all the parts into the PCB, choosing a generic Alpha 9mm pot footprint for all the pots. I also added a bunch of these empty pads for the off-board parts, and for the ground connection to the sleeve of the input jack (this build uses a copper ground area as well as a ground star mesh for the other components).

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/bc67e0cbccef86e7fb7f7bb412c705609805cdb4582635919306f5337148b854.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/dd01b65c410ccbeea5fbea1de630bb2ea22bb44dcb1b80060bd05a0c7b622c86.png)

Then came placing all the components. I really wanted to make sure I put them all in sensible places, but I think (and hope) I did a pretty decent job. I was very pleased with my routing though - I'm sure it's not perfect, but I think it's better than what I did on the macro pad! Having more space definitely helped. I'm glad I didn't try to squeeze this all into a tiny pre-made enclosure because that might have been tricky!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/f54d9afd34eb6e84b5ee357b909ba1ebdc30d7fd080a0352689ecd9f734994cc.png)

I did some fun silkscreening too, and it's looking pretty cool if I do say so myself! Managed to get the hack club logo on this time, and a little picture of the OG pedal.

Pretty much done now! Just need to do the project info, GitHub, admin etc.
